title: Understanding Life Insurance Surrender Value
description: Surrender value is the amount you receive if you terminate a life insurance policy before its full term. It is typically available only after paying premiums .

faq.q: What is surrender value in life insurance?
faq.a: Surrender value is the amount an insurance company pays you if you decide to terminate your life insurance policy before its maturity date. It is a portion of the premiums you've paid, minus certain charges.

faq.q: Is surrender value taxable in India?
faq.a: For policies issued before April 1, 2023, surrender value is tax-exempt under Section 10(10D) if annual premiums were within 10% (or 20% for older policies) of the sum assured. For policies issued on or after April 1, 2023, if the aggregate annual premium exceeds ₹5 lakh, the surrender value (profit component) becomes taxable.

faq.q: Can I surrender a life insurance policy anytime?
faq.a: No, you typically cannot surrender a policy anytime. Most traditional policies require a minimum of two or three full years of premium payments before a surrender value accrues. ULIPs have a mandatory five-year lock-in period.

faq.q: What is the difference between Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV) and Special Surrender Value (SSV)?
faq.a: GSV is a minimum, fixed percentage of premiums paid (excluding the first year and riders) guaranteed in your policy. SSV is often higher, calculated at the insurer's discretion based on factors like paid-up value, accrued bonuses, and market conditions, but it adheres to IRDAI guidelines.

faq.q: What happens if I stop paying premiums but don't surrender?
faq.a: If you stop paying premiums after the initial mandatory period, your policy might become 'paid-up'. This means the life cover continues with a reduced sum assured, and you won't need to pay further premiums, but you won't receive the full benefits originally planned.

faq.q: Is it advisable to surrender a life insurance policy?
faq.a: Generally, surrendering a life insurance policy is not advisable as it almost always results in a financial loss and the cessation of your life cover. It should be considered a last resort after exploring alternatives like making the policy paid-up or taking a policy loan.
